headline: The AI chatbot platform Character.AI has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy five years after it was founded, while agreeing to sell some assets to Disney.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a well-known consumer AI platform could be sold or shut down within weeks, confirmed by the company's own statement.
importance_line: Users of the platform could lose it if no workable bid comes in a sale expected to close in late November or early December, and TechCrunch reads the filing as a sign that consumer AI chat apps are hard to scale and make money from, because costs rise the more people use them; whether any bidder will appear is unknown.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Character.AI, whose platform lets users create AI characters and talk to them, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy (a US court process that lets a company keep trading while it restructures or sells assets) after a series of lawsuits and difficulty scaling, listing assets and liabilities of between $50 million and $100 million, and has agreed to sell some assets to Disney for $20 million together with a non-exclusive perpetual licence to its technology. Character.AI chief executive Colin Adams said the company will keep operating during a sale process expected to close in late November or early December, but there is no bid or buyer yet, and the platform "will be wound down" if no workable proposal comes.
